# SEO-226: Mark decorative images with an empty alt attribute

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `images` |
| Category | `ACCESSIBILITY` |
| Minimum level | `LITE` |
| Severity | `MEDIUM` |

| Change safety | `SAFE_AUTOMATIC` |
| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

An image that adds no information a reader needs - a background texture, a spacer, a repeated ornament, an icon beside text that already says the same thing - carries an alt attribute present but empty rather than absent.

## Rationale

An absent attribute makes assistive technology fall back to announcing the file name, so the reader is read a URL instead of being allowed to skip an element that carried nothing.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_images"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Decide per image whether it informs or decorates, and set the empty attribute only for the decorative case. Where the image is purely presentational, moving it into CSS removes the question entirely.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Report images whose alt attribute is absent, separating those that duplicate adjacent text or serve as ornament from those that carry content.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `ACCESSIBILITY_SCAN`, `FILE`
- Automated check: none.
